title: {MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR} template used by the too-far-future scenario is not defined anywhere in the SKILL.md runner contract
evidence: Scenario: `desired_move_in_date: "{MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR}"`. SKILL.md step 4 (line 172) enumerates only `{RUN_ID}`, `{SHORT_CODE}`, `{SCENARIO}`, `{TIMESTAMP}`, `- `{MOVE_IN_DATE}` → today + 90 days as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. `date -v+90d +%F`)` — a repo-wide grep for MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR matches only the scenario YAML itself. SKILL.md line 278 also still says "Only the boundary-validation scenarios (`desired-move-in-date-in-past`, `-too-far-future`) pin literal dates on purpose", which now contradicts the scenario.
detail: The runner substitutes only documented templates, so the token stays literal, the server hits the date parse-failure branch (which the scenario description explicitly disclaims), and the scenario passes while silently never exercising the 12-month upper-bound branch it exists to pin. Unit test `validate_move_in_date_too_far_future_test` (application_handler_test.gleam:413) still pins that branch, hence note not warning.
recommended_fix: Document `{MOVE_IN_DATE_TOO_FAR}` (today + 13 months, YYYY-MM-DD) in SKILL.md step 4 and the templates section, and fix the stale 'pin literal dates' sentence to name only `desired-move-in-date-in-past`.
